en.title: Exact Number of Configurations Under Running and Waiting Thresholds
en.description:
Each robot has its own identity and is in exactly one state, running or waiting. A running robot requires the total number of running robots r≥its own threshold; a waiting robot requires the total number of waiting robots n−r to be strictly less than its own threshold. Find the number of valid identity configurations, without taking any modulus.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; additions for bounds missing from the sources and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n and the second line contains n thresholds. The original bounds are 1≤n≤100000, 1≤a[i]≤n. The original int return signature cannot hold the actual result, so this site explicitly outputs an arbitrary-precision decimal integer of up to about 30103 digits.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 2; 1; and 4, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Let the frequency prefix F(t) count the thresholds ≤t. Fix r. When r≤n−r, check the forbidden middle zone and the forced counts; otherwise let M=F(r)−F(n−r) and K=r−F(n−r), which contributes C(M,K). As r increases, neither M nor K decreases, so update in batches with the recurrence between adjacent binomial coefficients instead of recomputing comb for every r.
